defense.why_it_works: Oracle services ship with well-known default credentials: Oracle 9 uses 'CHANGE_ON_INSTALL' as the default password, and the Oracle DBSNMP service uses 'dbsnmp'. These defaults are frequently left unchanged, giving attackers immediate access.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the Oracle TNS listener (TCP 1521).
defense.impact: SID/service names and, via well-known default credentials, database access.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046 AN1583] Monitor for execution of network enumeration utilities (nmap, netcat, net.exe, ping.exe, tracert.exe) in short succession, particularly when chained with lateral movement tools or system enumeration commands. [AN1584] Sequential ping, arp, or traceroute commands issued from bash scripts or interactive shells to map remote hosts are a strong behavioral indicator.
defense.artifacts: TNS listener connection and query entries in Oracle listener logs.
defense.prevention:
Change all default Oracle passwords immediately after installation — SYS, SYSTEM, DBSNMP, and all other built-in accounts. Oracle includes a built-in encryption mechanism for data transmission; ensure it is enabled. Audit and lock/disable unused Oracle accounts.

[MITRE T1046 M1042] Disable or remove unnecessary services and functionality that expose attack surface. [M1030] Implement network segmentation to limit the set of hosts reachable from any given compromised system. Use firewalls to restrict which source addresses can reach each service port.
defense.misconfiguration: Services expose excessive information: version banners, supported auth methods, valid usernames via error responses. IPMI has no authentication (version 2.0 cipher 0 vulnerability). RSH/rexec trust .rhosts files. rsync shares readable anonymously. Oracle TNS allows remote poisoning in older versions.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# IPMI cipher 0 — no authentication required:
# ipmitool -H <ip> -U admin -P '' -I lanplus -C 0 chassis status
# Returns valid data — auth bypassed entirely

# rsync anonymous access:
# rsync --list-only rsync://<ip>/  # lists all modules without auth
# rsync rsync://<ip>/backup /tmp   # downloads backup files

# Oracle TNS — version banner reveals exact version:
# nmap -p 1521 -sV -> Oracle Database 11.2.0.4 (exact version)
defense.secure_config:
# IPMI — disable cipher 0, enable only strong ciphers:
# /etc/ipmi/ipmievd.conf: IPMI_CIPHER_SUITE=17  (AES, mandatory auth)
# Or disable IPMI entirely if not needed (BMC IPMI = critical attack surface)

# rsync — require auth:
# /etc/rsyncd.conf:
# [backup]
#   auth users = backupuser
#   secrets file = /etc/rsyncd.secrets
#   hosts allow = 10.10.1.0/24

# RSH/rexec — disable entirely (replaced by SSH):
systemctl disable rsh.socket rexec.socket rlogin.socket

# Oracle TNS — disable remote admin, enforce auth:
# sqlnet.ora: SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES = (BEQ, TCPS)  (not NONE)
